minutes.headline: ZBA granted both special permits (a lot-width reduction on Arbor Street, a front setback on Island Road) and set new fees.
minutes.summary: The board heard two special permit applications and granted both by voice vote. It also discussed new application fees and settled on keeping the residential filing fee, adding a higher commercial fee, and making applicants pay advertising and abutter postage, to be reviewed in six months. A third scheduled hearing (a kennel) was withdrawn.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment on the Arbor Street application; none came from the floor or Zoom.
Chair asked for public comment on the Island Road application; none came from the floor or Zoom.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit as requested for 155 Arbor Street, reducing lot width through the building.
votes.outcome: passed (spoken ayes; count not stated, no opposition heard)

votes.motion: Grant the special permit for a front setback of 23.5 ft at 48 Island Road.
votes.outcome: passed (spoken ayes; count not stated, no opposition heard)

votes.motion: Set fees at $100 residential and $150 commercial, with applicant paying advertising and abutter postage, to be reviewed in six months.

budget_items.what_was_said: Secretary presented fee comparisons from surrounding towns; the current filing fee is out of date and has not been raised in decades.
The proposal shifts advertising and abutter postage to the applicant, since the town has been losing money on each application and transferring money to cover a deficit.
Members discussed a higher commercial fee on account of longer, more detailed hearings. Staff cautioned that fees must reflect actual town cost.
Members raised needing tablets to review plans once online permitting begins; no money is in the budget now.
Fees set as residential unchanged and a higher commercial fee, with applicant paying advertising and postage, reviewed in six months.

transfers.description: Staff said last year's deficit required repeated transfers of money to cover application costs; the new fee structure would eliminate that.

decisions.decision: The kennel application at 1295 Massachusetts Avenue was withdrawn by letter, so no hearing was held.
Fee structure to be revisited in six months once online permitting provides workload data.
Online ZBA permitting goes live as soon as the meeting ends; paper copies of large plans for board members are unresolved until equipment is available.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit at 155 Arbor Street to reduce lot width through the building, by voice vote.
The board granted a special permit for a front setback reduction at 48 Island Road, by voice vote.
The board set new application fees: the residential fee kept, a higher commercial fee added, and applicants to pay advertising and abutter postage.
The fee structure is to be reviewed in six months, once online permitting provides workload data.
A kennel application at 1295 Massachusetts Avenue was withdrawn by letter, so no hearing was held.

why_it_matters: Applicants, not the town, now carry the cost of advertising and abutter mailings, which the discussion said the town had been covering at a loss on each application.
Online permitting begins when the meeting ends, and board members' tablets to review plans have no money in the current budget, so a small equipment request may follow.
